sentences.text: Smt. Deepa Devi D/o Shri Chhok Nath W/o Late Ded Nath, aged about 55 years, R/o Bidasar, Distt. Churu Raj.
----Petitioner  Versus 1. State of Rajasthan
2. Smt. Jyani Devi W/o Late Ded Nath, R/o Village-  Ghantiyal Badi, Tehsil- Bidasar, Distt. Churu Raj.

----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Hitendra Singh For Respondent(s) : Mr. Vikram Singh Rajpurohit, PP  Mr. V.S. Choudhary  Mr. Rohit Singh for respondent No.2  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP TANEJA Order 08/10/2025 1.

By way of filing the instant misc. petition, petitioner has laid challenge to the order dated 29.06.2016 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Sujangarh (for short 'the learned trial court'), vide which, cognizance was taken against the petitioner for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC and as also to the order dated 04.11.2016 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Sujangarh (for short 'the learned revisional court') in Criminal Revision No.28/2015, whereby the order dated 29.06.2016 has been affirmed.
2. Brief facts of the case are that the respondent No.2 submitted a compliant, which was sent for investigation under Section 156(3) CrPC to the Police Station Chhapar.
An FIR was registered against the petitioner and other persons.

It was alleged (Uploaded on 10/10/2025 at 12:41:08 PM)
(2 of 3) [CRLMP-3556/2016] that deceased husband of the complainant Late Ded Nath had 1/28th share in the joint khatedari land falling in Khasra No.139 situated in Kothinada, Tehsil Sujangarh.

In order to grab the land, the petitioner along with others fabricated the documents and got her name entered in the revenue record as legal heir of deceased Ded Nath, whereas she is legally wedded wife of Ramnath.
3. The police after thorough investigation into the matter, filed a negative final report.
4. The respondent No.2, thereafter, filed a protest petition and her statements were recorded under Sections 200 and 202 CrPC.

sentences.text: The learned trial court vide order dated 29.06.2016 rejected the negative final report and allowed the protest petition filed by the respondent No.2.
Vide the said order, the learned trial court took cognizance against the petitioner for the offences under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC.
Cognizance was also taken against other accused persons as well.
6. The petitioner, by way of filing revision petition, challenged the said order of cognizance before the learned revisional court, which came to be dismissed vide impugned order dated 04.11.2016.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the learned trial court has committed error in taking cognizance against the petitioner as there is no material on record so as to make out a prima facie case against the petitioner.
It is further submitted that the learned revisional court also did not consider the material available on record in right perspective and simply upheld the order passed by the learned trial court.

On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel for the complainant supported the impugned orders and submitted that both the courts below have not committed any error as the orders have been passed after taking into consideration the material available on record.
9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the impugned orders passed by learned revisional court and learned trial court.

Learned trial court has held that there is prima facie evidence available on record to proceed against the accused for committing offences under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC and the same has carefully been examined by the learned revisional court.

10. In view of the concurrent findings of both the learned courts and in view of the fact that both the learned courts, while arriving at their findings, have properly considered the material available on record including the material placed by the Investigating Agency, this Court does not find any ground to interfere with the impugned orders in exercise of the powers conferred under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
11.
Accordingly, the criminal misc. petition as well as stay petition are dismissed.
12. However, the petitioner is at liberty to take all her defence at appropriate stage.

(SANDEEP TANEJA),J 60 - ms rathore (Uploaded on 10/10/2025 at 12:41:08 PM) Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
